name: commit-proves-order
title: The Commit Has to Prove the Order
kicker: git pre-commit reads the log, line by line
html:
The Commit Has to Prove the Order

A Feature File, First?

Before the first production write.

A Failing Run, Before the Code?

Red, logged, before that write.

Green, Last?

The final run passed.

Any “no”, and there’s no commit, whoever is committing.

pre-commit

The commit

e3dbaca4 · 11 Nov 2026

The library’s rules come from its policy file, and the simulator serves the library alone by one, as a preview

7 files: the feature, its steps, the policy, and where it’s used.
say: Last step: the commit. And here the git pre-commit hook reads the log since the last commit, in order. Did a feature file change before the first production write? Was there a failing run before that write? Was the last run green? If any answer is no, there's no commit, whoever is committing: Claude, me, anyone. This one passed. It's commit e3dbaca4, on the 11th of November: the library's rules come from its policy file. Seven files, the feature, its steps, the policy and the three places that use it. One sentence from me; one behavior, in the right order, on the record.
